title: AlphaFold 3: Predicting Biomolecular Interactions
hook: AlphaFold 3 extends protein structure prediction to full biomolecular complexes - proteins with DNA, RNA, ligands, and ions - using a diffusion-based architecture.
key_points: Predicts joint 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, small molecules, and ions in one model.
Replaces AlphaFold 2's hand-crafted structure modules with a diffusion process over atomic coordinates.
Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on protein-ligand docking, a key task in drug discovery.
Abramson et al. at Google DeepMind published results in Nature alongside a limited public server.
content_html: Abramson and colleagues at Google DeepMind published AlphaFold 3 in Nature in May 2024. Where AlphaFold 2 focused on single-chain protein structures, AlphaFold 3 jointly models entire biomolecular assemblies - proteins alongside DNA, RNA, small-molecule ligands, and metal ions.
extra_html:
How it works

The architecture swaps out AlphaFold 2's Evoformer-plus-structure-module pipeline for a diffusion model that directly generates atomic coordinates. A Pairformer module (an updated Evoformer variant) processes pairwise representations of all atoms, and the diffusion process iteratively refines the full 3D assembly from noise to a predicted structure.

Why it matters

Being able to predict how a drug-like molecule binds to a target protein - with the full protein-ligand complex modeled at once - is a long-standing bottleneck in early-stage drug discovery. AlphaFold 3's strong performance on this task makes it a practical tool for medicinal chemistry, not just an academic benchmark. Read the full paper in Nature for accuracy breakdowns across molecule types.
